name: Middle Aortic Syndrome

criteria.description: Segmental narrowing or hypoplasia of the distal thoracic or abdominal aorta
Severe, often refractory hypertension, especially in young patients
Presence of extensive collateral arterial circulation on imaging
Stenosis or involvement of renal arteries contributing to hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of segmental aortic narrowing with associated hypertension confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings combined with clinical hypertension; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features are present.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental narrowing of the distal thoracic or abdominal aorta
pathognomonic.notes: Identified by imaging modalities such as CT angiography or MRI
searchTerms: narrowed section of large chest or belly artery
segmental aorta narrowing in thorax or abdomen

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe refractory hypertension in childhood or young adulthood
pathognomonic.notes: Often resistant to multiple antihypertensive agents
searchTerms: severe high blood pressure resistant to treatment

common.symptomName: Lower limb claudication due to decreased distal perfusion
searchTerms: leg pain when walking due to poor blood flow
muscle cramps in legs with activity

common.notes: Pulse discrepancy between upper and lower extremities
searchTerms: weak or missing pulses in upper thigh
reduced blood flow pulses in legs

common.notes: Common presenting symptom related to elevated blood pressure
searchTerms: headaches caused by high blood pressure

common.symptomName: Renovascular hypertension due to renal artery stenosis
common.notes: May contribute to overall hypertension severity
searchTerms: high blood pressure from narrowed kidney artery

occasional.notes: Audible turbulent blood flow over stenotic segments

occasional.symptomName: Left ventricular hypertrophy secondary to chronic hypertension
searchTerms: thickened heart muscle from high blood pressure
left heart enlargement due to hypertension
episodes of lightheadedness or passing out

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue due to decreased distal perfusion
searchTerms: tiredness from poor blood flow to limbs

rare.symptomName: Mesenteric ischemia symptoms such as postprandial abdominal pain
rare.notes: Due to involvement of visceral arteries
searchTerms: belly pain after eating from poor blood flow

rare.symptomName: Renal insufficiency secondary to chronic renal artery stenosis
rare.notes: May progress to chronic kidney disease if untreated
searchTerms: kidney problems from chronic artery narrowing
renal insufficiency due to artery stenosis
kidney function decline from blood flow loss

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine if renal artery stenosis causes renal impairment
Normal inflammatory markers unless associated with vasculitis
imaging: CT angiography or MR angiography showing segmental narrowing of the distal thoracic or abdominal aorta
Collateral arterial circulation visible on angiography
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromes like neurofibromatosis type 1 or Williams syndrome in some cases
other: Blood pressure discrepancy between upper and lower limbs

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic symptoms such as fever and malaise
Involvement of aortic arch branches more common
Typically involves aortic isthmus just distal to left subclavian artery
Usually diagnosed in infancy or childhood
Characteristic rib notching on chest X-ray

redFlags: Severe refractory hypertension in young patients
Absent or diminished lower limb pulses
Signs of end-organ damage such as hypertensive encephalopathy or renal failure
references: Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2019: Clinical features and management of Middle Aortic Syndrome
